marketDemographics.note: 2-mile ring: pop 30,893 / avg HH income $212,741. Average home value 1-mile $1,118,348; 3-mile $796,833. Placer.ai trade area (top 70% of visitors): pop 308,169 / avg HH income $141,071.

deals.shadowAnchors: Three outparcels (Chevron, Wells Fargo, Citibank) sit on separately-owned parcels bound to the center by a reciprocal easement agreement; they are NOT part of the 139,913 SF GLA. Outparcels reimburse the owner via fixed annual payments that step up 15% every 5 years.

deals.notes: Regency Court at Woodfield is a 139,913 SF, Publix- and Walgreens-anchored community center built in 1992 on ±14.85 acres at the signalized corner of Yamato Rd & Jog Rd (±77,500 VPD) at the entrance to Woodfield Country Club in central Boca Raton (Boca Raton West submarket). The trade area is exceptionally affluent — 1-mile average HH income of $264,527 and average home value of $1,118,348 (90% / 73% above Palm Beach County). Publix (#0428, 42,112 SF) is a standout at $46.1M / $1,095 PSF in 2025 (13% above Publix's chain average) on a low $7.50 PSF base + 1% percentage rent over a $31.58M breakpoint, with a ~1.9% health ratio. Both anchors are original 1992 tenants paying well below market (Publix ~58% below, Walgreens ~45% below) and fully expire within ~6 years (Publix current 12/9/2027 plus one 5-yr option to Dec-2032; Walgreens 11/30/2031), driving the value-add thesis: mark-to-market of 81,543 SF (67% of occupied GLA, >$1.0M upside), lease-up of 13,927 SF of vacancy (10% of GLA), and anchor renewal/expansion (Publix has discussed a 47,240 SF expansion) or re-tenanting. The OM projects 94% NOI growth over a 10-year hold (6.8% CAGR) off an In-Place NOI of $3,651,460; T-12 (Apr-25–Mar-26) actual NOI was $2,965,093 on $5.16M income and $2.20M opex. Shops are high-performing and seasoned (avg shop sales $651 PSF, 9.1% health ratio, 14.5-yr tenure). Debt-free and offered unpriced by CBRE National Retail Partners; key risks are concentrated near-term anchor rollover, Walgreens' BB- credit and soft reported sales, and a Chase co-tenancy tied to Publix occupancy.
keyAssumptions: In-Place NOI of $3,651,460 is the OM's normalized in-place figure; T-12 actual NOI (Apr-25–Mar-26) was $2,965,093 (Total Income $5,164,899 − OpEx $2,199,807). The ~$686K gap reflects vacancy gross-up, reimbursement normalization, and removal of bad debt/concessions.
No asking price or guidance cap rate stated — the asset is being offered unpriced / best-offer by CBRE NRP.

Publix current lease expiration is 12/9/2027 with ONE automatic 5-year option (auto-exercises unless Publix gives 6 months' notice) to 12/9/2032; the OM's 'fully expires Dec-2032' reflects the option period.

DETAILED RENT ROLL IS IMAGE-BASED: the OM rent-roll pages (49–58) are scanned images that yield NO extractable text, so per-tenant base rents and lease dates were taken from the OM's Mark-to-Market table and Publix abstract ONLY. Rents/expiries are populated where a tenant's SF maps UNIQUELY; same-SF tenants (several 1,606 / 1,423 / 1,063 SF shops) are left null and must be confirmed against the rent roll, Argus file, or a structured rent-roll upload.

ANCHOR TERMS VERIFIED AGAINST EXECUTED LEASES (folder '7) Anchor Leases'): Publix automatic-extension letter (4/6/2022) confirms the term runs 12/10/2022–12/9/2027 with 1 remaining 5-year option (→12/9/2032); Walgreens recorded Memorandum & Ratification (1992) confirms the term runs 12/1/1991–11/30/2031 and the premises are 12,422 SF. The tenant-sales report's 12,233 SF denominator is therefore superseded — use 12,422 SF.
Tax bill figures (assessed $42,205,863; ad valorem $688,917 + non-ad-valorem $124,038 = $812,955) are per the 2025 Palm Beach County bill, stated net of a 4% early-payment discount.

redFlags.description: Concentrated near-term anchor rollover: Publix (42,112 SF, 30% of GLA) and Walgreens (12,422 SF) BOTH fully expire within ~6 years (Publix current 12/9/2027 / option to Dec-2032; Walgreens 11/30/2031). The value-add thesis depends on renewing/re-tenanting both at much higher rents — execution and downtime risk.
10% vacancy (13,927 SF across suites A014, B020-22, C006, C007) — lease-up cost/time risk; the In-Place NOI assumes this space contributes.

Walgreens credit is BB- (S&P, below investment grade) and its REPORTED sales are low/declining ($197.84 PSF in 2025 vs $218.82 in 2024); the OM adjusts to an estimated $822 PSF by adding back 3rd-party-plan Rx sales excluded from reported figures — the reported figure is the contractual basis.

Chase Bank (B022-24) co-tenancy/go-dark: Chase may cease operating if Publix is vacant 90+ days, with base rent abating until ≥75% of the Publix premises is re-occupied by a single retailer; after one year of reduced rent Chase must terminate or resume full rent — anchor-dependent income risk during any Publix transition.

Anchor income is well below market and partly percentage-rent dependent (Publix base just $7.50 PSF + 1% over a $31.58M breakpoint); in-place yield is low relative to a trophy price — returns rely on realizing the mark-to-market.

Environmental: property enrolled in Florida's Dry Cleaning Solvent program (former dry cleaner, Suite B012). Aug-2025 report met No Further Action criteria and FDEP confirmed closure 12/15/2025, but the formal Site Rehabilitation Completion Order (SRCO) and site restoration were still pending as of the OM.
Data completeness: detailed per-tenant rents/dates for in-line shops are not in the OM's extractable text (image-based rent roll) — confirm the full rent roll before underwriting.

upsideItems.detail: 81,543 SF (67% of occupied GLA), incl. Publix and Walgreens, is ~36% below market (current avg $22.88 vs market $35.59 PSF) — >$1.0M of identified rent upside realizable over a 10-year hold.
13,927 SF (10% of GLA) of available space in an infill, 98.4%-occupied submarket with shop asking rents of $45–$55 PSF NNN.

Publix is below market at $7.50 PSF and has expressed interest in waiving its remaining option and renewing early, and in an expanded 47,240 SF prototype store — new South FL grocer rents are mid-to-upper $20s PSF.
Option to renew Walgreens at market, re-tenant the 12,422 SF box, or convert/divide it into higher-rent shop space; Walgreens has relocation rights.
In-place leases carry contractual increases that contribute to the projected 94% / 6.8% CAGR 10-year NOI growth.
